data.body:
Somewhere along the way, clear skin became shorthand for discipline, health, even virtue. It is none of those. It is skin.

If you are tired of being sold your own insecurity, you are in the right place.
data.heading: Skincare is not self-worth

data.body: Three things the industry would rather you forget.
data.heading: What skincare actually is — and isn't

cards.description: The pressure is quiet but constant: a breakout reads as a failure, a wrinkle as neglect. That framing sells product, and it borrows your self-worth as collateral. You can decline the loan.
cards.title: A breakout is not a failure

cards.description: Skin responds to genes, hormones, sleep, stress, and age — most of which you do not control. A good routine helps at the margins. It cannot measure whether you are trying hard enough as a person.
cards.title: Skin reflects biology, not effort

cards.description: Care for your skin the way you would care for a houseplant: attentively, kindly, and without moral stakes. It will do better, and so will you.
cards.title: Care without moral stakes

data.body: Start with the essay this page is built on, then explore the rest of the library at your own pace.
data.heading: Want the calmer way of thinking about skin?

seo.description: Caring for your skin is fine. Tying your value to it is not the same thing. A calm, honest take for anyone tired of the skincare industry's guilt.
seo.title: Skincare Is Not Self-Worth
